questions.prompt: You observe `Get-WmiObject` in a PowerShell script. What does this tell you about the target environment?

options.a: The script targets legacy PowerShell 5.1 (Get-WmiObject was removed in PS7 in favor of Get-CimInstance)
options.b: The script is written specifically for Linux cross-platform pwsh 7
options.c: The script requires administrator privileges to execute

questions.prompt: Why is WMI/CIM frequently leveraged by attackers during post-exploitation (T1047)?

options.a: It provides native capabilities for system recon, process execution (Win32_Process.Create), and fileless persistence
options.c: It encrypts all hard drive contents

questions.prompt: What happens when `Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem` is executed on pwsh 7 on Linux?

options.a: It returns errors or empty output because WMI/CIM is Windows-only (no CIM repository on Linux)
options.b: It reads Linux system information from /proc/sys
